goal: Look at the digit blocks on the table (4 or 5 of them) and place them on the row of mats so that, read in order along the row, they form the largest possible number (largest digit on the first mat, smallest on the last), then return the arm home.
instruction_templates: Arrange the numbers from left to right to form the largest possible number, and place them on the pad.
success: Let n be the number of digit blocks (4 or 5, labels digit_0..digit_{n-1}); each shows a digit d = model_id % 10, all distinct (unique sampling). Sort the blocks by digit value descending: the block with the largest digit must be placed on mat_0, the next largest on mat_1, ..., the smallest on mat_{n-1}. This yields the largest possible number when read in mat order.

Mats mat_0..mat_{n-1} are fixed cushions in a row along world x with spacing 0.085 m, centred at x=0, shared y drawn in [-0.10,-0.05] m; mat_0 has the smallest x (x = (i-(n-1)/2)*0.085). Position check per block: xy (horizontal) Euclidean distance from the digit block's root origin to its assigned mat's root origin must be < 0.02 m (z ignored).

Orientation per block, every angle strictly < 45 degrees: (a) the block's local +y axis aligned with world +y; for digit 0 either local +y or local -y aligned with world +y is accepted; (b) for every digit except 0 and 8, the block's local +x axis aligned with world +x. So 8 needs only (a); 0 needs only the relaxed (a); digits 1-7 and 9 need both (a) and (b). Which local axes correspond to the block's printed face/orientation is not determinable statically; effectively the block must be placed roughly upright with its text reading direction within 45 degrees of the nominal one (in-plane rotation less than 45 degrees, not tipped on its side).
All target robots back at episode-start end-effector pose: |dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m and rotation diff <= 20 degrees (all_robot_back_to_origin defaults).
evaluation: Checked after every action (each action = one call to take_action; the reward manager step runs after the action's control sequence has finished executing). A single stage: all per-block position and orientation conditions for all n blocks plus 'robots back at origin' must hold simultaneously at one step; the first such step ends the episode with success. There is no early-failure rule except the generic ones (physics instability/layout invalid). Otherwise the episode fails at step_lim=1050 actions. The process get_score (transition mode, scores [5,15,30,100] for 4 digits or [5,15,25,40,100] for 5 digits) is only a partial-credit metric: stage k needs all grippers open (open fraction >= 0.8) and any k blocks correctly placed; not required for success.
objects: digit_0..digit_{n-1}: number blocks (category 'number'), n = 4 or 5 chosen per episode; model ids 0-9 (one of three texture groups texture0/1/2 per episode: ids 0-9, 10-19 or 20-29; the digit shown = id % 10), unique digits; scattered on the table x in [-0.4,0.4], y in [-0.25,-0.05] (m), random yaw within +/-45 deg, 0.015 m margin; keep-out area x[-0.01,0.01], y[-0.20,-0.15].
mat_0..mat_{n-1}: cushions (Geometry, cube_cushion index 1), one per digit block, in a row along x with 0.085 m spacing centred at x=0, shared y in [-0.10,-0.05], no rotation.
needs_memory_or_language: The agent must read the digit on each block from vision (the digit is the model identity, only visible as the number texture; the reward uses model_id % 10) and order them: largest digit to mat_0 (lowest x). Which end is 'left' is, per the code, the mat with smallest world x, mat_0 (the instruction says 'left to right'; confirm orientation from the camera).
end_requirements: All target arms back at start pose within 0.15 m per axis and 20 degrees at the moment the last block is correctly placed (no gripper-state requirement in the success check).
notes:
Block-to-mat assignment is deterministic: sorted by digit descending, so the order is unique. Digit orientation checks are loose (<45 deg), but the position tolerance is tight (0.02 m xy from the mat's origin). The 8 only needs +y up (< 45 deg), 0 accepts +y or -y, others need both +y and +x. Which digits appear (and how many, 4 vs 5) varies per episode. Digits and mats are identified at runtime by labels digit_i / mat_i, not by digit value, so labels digit_i do not carry the digit value. The success condition has no 'not grasped' or 'gripper open' condition.
Identical reward to arrange_largest_number_random; this variant has no clutter.
